about: Accepted faults and author decisions collected while finishing V15 chapters 1 to 8 (2026-10-01). Art faults here used their correction attempts or sit in approved art; each needs an author decision (accept, or regenerate later).

items.fault: Accepted fault for the author list: Ibrahim still shows a faint diagonal scar mark on his RIGHT cheek (the image-left side of his face, in front of his visible ear). The v03 edit made it lighter than in v02, but it was not removed, and the LEFT-side scar is not shown.

Accepted faults for the author's list (v03, the latest edit, is v02 with these marks only slightly softened): (1) Ibrahim's forehead ash still reads as three soft horizontal white stripes just below the turban, not one thumb smear. (2) The seated official on the far platform still has a small dark-red dot at the centre of his forehead; the script says no forehead marks. (3) Minor: Ibrahim's scar is a thin pale line on his visible LEFT cheek that runs from below the ear toward the corner of the moustache rather than down to the jaw. It is on the correct side.

Accepted faults for the author list. (1) Ibrahim still has two short pale-white dashes on his RIGHT cheek (screen-left, just below the eye). The v03 edit did not remove them. (2) His forehead ash is a small pale rectangular patch with faint horizontal striping, just below the turban, not one soft thumb smear. This is better than v02's two distinct white stripes but still not a smear.

v03 is acceptable and matches the evening lamplit hall. The setting is right: a dark carved back wall, open brass oil lamps on chains and a standing brass lamp, an unlettered silver-conch-on-red standard, bare-headed Nair guards with topknots and crossed belts, and topknotted seated men. The official is seen from behind with a topknot and white shoulder cloth. Nagoji is correct: clean chin, thick curled moustache, hair tied back, cream tunic-shirt, bandaged wrists, barefoot, eyes on the official. Ibrahim wears no coat, only the cream vest over a white shirt and white mundu, with his turban and grey-flecked beard. The plain ochre wall band across the top is clear for the three balloons. For the author list: (1) Ibrahim's forehead ash is still two pale horizontal stripes, not one faint smear. v03 is acceptable and is now evening. The brass oil lamps light the room, the walls are warm ochre, and the far-left window shows a dusk sky with palm silhouettes, so it matches 8.1 and the earlier hall panels. The official is at the right on his raised seat, at a readable size, with a slight smile, a topknot, a clean chin, a bare torso and the stylus over the leaf. Nagoji makes a measured standing bow in the left foreground: clean chin, curled moustache, gold ear ornament, hair tied at the nape, bandaged wrists. Ibrahim stands a step behind him with no coat. The large plain wall beside and above the official is free for both official balloons. The captions can sit on the wall between Nagoji's lowered head and the pillar, or on the floor below. items.fault: A background prisoner has Nagoji's markers (curly hair, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud); minor (r13 review).
Keshavrao's arms are flung wide with no chain between his wrist manacles; the chapter's irons call for a forearm-long chain (r9 review).
The broadside wave beat reads weakly: a level, untilted hold rather than men thrown sideways (r9 review).

Panels 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.5 are narrowed to about 78 percent of the column and centred while 3.4 runs full width; choose tighter crops to fill the width, or one shared width for every panel on a page (r9 review).

The caption 'The dungeon had scraped that away.' sits across the Chaul memory inset (young Keshavrao on the bay horse). Page 5 cannot fit its five panels' lettering: the script makes 5.4 full width and 5.5 the full-width, tallest panel, which leaves 5.2 about 66 pt tall. Options: accept the overlap, let 5.5 be shorter than its full-width height, or shorten or move one 5.2 caption.
'Horses would hate this.' now reads last at the bottom left of 3.3, in script order, but no longer sits on the feet inset it jokes about.

Keshavrao faces the camera and turns fully to stare at Nagoji; the script wants him seen from behind, head turned only a few degrees, eyes forward ('a friend who will not look back'), right hand curled at the hip round an absent hilt. Needs a regeneration if the author wants the beat.
Page 1's tiers have three different widths and none fills the column (same question as chapter 3 page 3): tighter crops to fill the width, or one shared width per page.
A tiny background musketeer in a blue coat and gold-edged tricorne reads as a Dutch blue-coat, against the rule for Portuguese guards; recolour or paint out on a later pass.

The brand is drawn differently in each panel (angry puckered patch in 3.2, lacy blotch in 5.4, four pale curved lines like whip marks in 6.5). A later pass could redraw 6.5 (and 5.4) as a paler version of the 3.2 patch.
A small white lace-like pattern on the outer side of Nagoji's left forearm reads as a scuff or salt crust at print size; clean it back to plain skin on a retouch pass.
The background wreck shows bare ribs close inshore, like an old rotted hulk rather than the fresh wreck of 2.4.

items.source: ch08 round 3 selection (accepted after two correction attempts)
items.fault: After two correction attempts: the hand at the belt is drawn as a right hand (thumb on the inner side, next to the buckle) on the LEFT arm, and the nails do not clearly show ridges. Logged for the author (v02 has the brand near the elbow on the outer forearm instead).

Script 12.4 now starts 'Full width.' (accepted revision, backup scripts/CHAPTER-07-SCRIPT.md.backup-pre-124-fullwidth): at half width beside 12.3 there was no room in the dusk sky for Ibrahim's long line without covering Nagoji. Revert if you prefer the pairing; the line would then need shortening.
The child beside the whispering girl still wears an olive short-sleeved stitched top (the girl's own blouse was fixed); an edit could drape her in cream cloth too.

The top tier of page 5 is ragged: 5.2 is fitted to its art's aspect and centred, so it is shorter than 5.1 beside it, with cream bands above and below. Same question as chapter 2 page 1 and chapter 3 page 3.

Accepted layout-cue revisions (backup scripts/CHAPTER-05-SCRIPT.md.backup-pre-11-85-layout): 1.1 'Wide' became 'Wide, full width' so the establishing shot spans the column; 8.5 'the tallest tier' gained 'about 40 percent of the page' so the closing panel is the tallest, with sky for its four captions.

Accepted layout-cue revision (backup scripts/CHAPTER-06-SCRIPT.md.backup-pre-82-size): 8.2 'the page's biggest panel' gained 'full width' and 'about 40 percent of the page'; at half width two balloons hid the whole Chaul memory.

Varma's seat: the script and 2.2 have him cross-legged on a mat on a low wooden platform, but 2.1, 2.5, 6.1, 6.4, 9.5 and 10.2 show a tall carved throne on a stone dais. Choose one: accept the throne (then only 2.2 differs) or have the five or six throne panels edited to the low platform.

The left gatepost niche lamp still reads as a brass bowl in a small glass case (the edit did not remove it); about 40 px wide, a later targeted edit can turn it into an open flame in a bare stone niche.
A tiny, hazy whitewashed church-like building with a bell tower sits on the distant waterfront; the carter keeps a faint thin moustache (script: clean-shaven).

Accepted layout-cue revision (backup scripts/CHAPTER-08-SCRIPT.md.backup-pre-113-fullwidth): 11.3 now starts 'Full width.' so Nagoji's line and Padmini's two lines fit in the sky; at half width beside 11.4 her second tail had to cross her first balloon.

The redrawn gaunt Wary Fisherman (v11) could only be lettered by letting the first balloon sit across part of the carry (Nagoji's body), since the fisherman's and Nagoji's faces are close together; the identity fix was judged worth more.

Page 12 cannot be lettered as written: 12.1 (175 characters) and 12.2 (181) and 12.4 (126) need trimming to about 100, 100 and 90 characters. The author is trimming the lines; a wording-change acceptance path will be added to the pipeline.

items.source: ch06 r1 review and tail workflow
items.fault: Ramayyan's order 'Take the Madurai horse...' still reads as Varma's: Varma's figure sits between every open space and Ramayyan, and a drawn tail stops before its target, so no lettering fixes it. Needs a regeneration per the script (from the entrance end, platform figures smaller, open wall near Ramayyan) or the lines moved.
Nagoji's tunic still shows a narrow neck band and a three-button placket (the edit that removed it also rewrote Ibrahim's vest, so the old pick was kept).

The script and the novel seat Varma on a mat on a slightly raised wooden platform, and 10.2's line ('too many lives to sit on that mat') leans on that image. 2.2 shows the mat; from 2.5 on he sits on a gilt lion-armed throne, on a stepped dais in 6.1 and 9.5. Accept the throne (he takes his seat for the audience), or regenerate the throne panels to the mat.

Page 11 holds more lettering than its art can carry (the panels need about 579 pt of height and the page has 520). See TRIM-SHEET-ch07-p12-ch08-p11-2026-10-02.html: shorten the lines, or split the page in two.

Page 8 holds about 986 characters of lettering; its panels need about 659 pt of height and the page has 517. r2 fitted only by shrinking the closing panel 8.5, which its review called a blocker. See the trim sheet: split the page (recommended, it is the chapter's last page) or shorten the lines.

Nagoji's two long hearsay lines fill the right half of the panel: the first balloon's tail ends on the padre in the stain, and the balloons hide the musketeer column and Varma's hand tapping the spear (both are drawn in the art). Keep zones and a body-aware tail rule could not free room; placing them clear makes the panel unplaceable. Fix options: shorten one or both lines, or regenerate the art with open smoke at the upper left for the lettering.

Ramayyan's order ('Take the Madurai horse...') sits left of the throne; its short tail ends near Varma's knee, so the king seems to speak it. No position at the right holds the line. Fix options: shorten the line so it fits under Ramayyan, or regenerate with Ramayyan nearer the open left side.

The ride to Velinadu shows Nagoji on a black horse with a white blaze, the same in every mounted panel. The bible gives him Kayal (bay mare, black mane and legs, no white) from chapter 7 on, and his plain grey gelding as a daytime mount in chapters 7 and 8. Keep the black horse, or edit the mounted panels to Kayal? Chapters 10 to 12 now name Kayal in every mounted panel.

A tiny gold bead still hangs just below the earlobe (3 to 6 px at full frame, barely visible in print) instead of the flush stud. Full-image edits and a region edit could not remove it; the model copies the drop from the nagoji-v2 sheet. Fix options: accept, or a hand retouch of those four ears.

Every version offers his RIGHT forearm, so the brand and scar sit on the right arm; the bible and your lock put them on the inner LEFT forearm. Recommended fix: flop (mirror) 11.4, a tight forearm-and-hand close-up where mirroring changes nothing else, and regenerate or flop 11.3 (flopping 11.3 would also move Revathi's bare shoulder to the wrong side). Your call.

The bared arm is his left, but the brand shows on the outer face of the forearm near mid-arm, with thin branching lines, rather than a puckered patch on the inner forearm a hand's width above the wrist.

Padmini stands in the lit doorway looking out at Nagoji rather than talking quietly with the elders behind her, and carries a sheathed sword in her left hand; a small red mark on her forehead is not on her sheet.

Your mat decision is done in every other throne panel, but in 9.5 Ramayyan's two lines ('Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders, and show him something there he has not already imagined.' and 'If you are wrong, you will find Travancore worse than the Portuguese.') do not fit in the open wall beside him in either mat version, so the build keeps the original throne frame for this one panel. Shorten one or both lines and the mat version (v04, ready) goes in.

Ibrahim has neither his ash nor his left-cheek scar here, and Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to the elbows, though they are down through the rest of the hall scene (7.1 to 9.1). Four versions exist; this is the best for the scene. Fix options: a local edit of Ibrahim's forehead and cheek and Nagoji's sleeves.

The official's '<You know their forts?>' and Nagoji's 'Some.' sit on each other's sides, so their tails cross in an X. Reading order (the four lines alternate speakers) forces the second pair after the first; face zones for both men are in place. Each tail still ends on its own speaker and the Malayalam angle brackets mark the official. Fix option: a hand re-letter swapping the two lower balloons.

The palm-leaf insert shows the stylus but no strokes being cut into the leaf, so the echo of the chapter 1 ledger (the name given back) does not read. Fix option: an edit adding fresh incised strokes under the stylus.

Nagoji, small at the back by the pillar, still has a tiny gold ring hanging below the ear stud (about 10 px). Also Varma sits on a carved chair on a red-carpeted platform rather than a plain low dais.
Faint stubble texture on Nagoji's jaw (reads as shading in print) and a sabre-style knuckle-guard hilt rather than a disc-pommel talwar; the blade is curved.
Nagoji's ear still shows a tiny gold oval hanging just below the lobe (a few pixels at print size). The long guns read as flintlocks rather than the matchlocks the script names.
Nagoji's ear shows a tiny gold hoop hanging just below the lobe (about 6 px in the 1536 px frame).
A faint flat skin-toned patch around the ear lobe and jaw left by the ear region edit (visible only at 4x zoom). Ramayyan walks beside Nagoji rather than waiting on the path.

The right sleeve sits a little above the right wrist, showing a short strip of bare right forearm (not the branded arm); framing is medium rather than a tight close. Regenerated after one moderation refusal.
A tiny gold drop on Nagoji's FAR ear, half hidden in his hair behind the jaw (about 5 by 10 px); his near ear is a correct flush stud. His boots are hidden behind the seat.

Revathi has a small dot between her brows below the sandalwood line (the bible allows only the line), wears a gold bead string rather than the flat-coin necklace, and sits just behind Padmini rather than farther back among the older women.
Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold bead at and just below the lobe edge (about 5 px), reading as a very small drop. Revathi has a tiny red dot between her brows; it appears in all three versions.
A full moon is drawn, while 21.1 and 21.4 show only stars; the nails are not clearly ridged and the brand edge reads as pale scar sheen at print size.
Ibrahim's horse is a mid bay here but dark brown in 18.1.

items.fault: Mirrored by author decision so the brand and scar sit on Nagoji's LEFT forearm. Side effects: Revathi's sari end now crosses her other shoulder (the bible has it over her LEFT shoulder), and screen direction flips against 12.1, 12.4 and 12.5 (here Nagoji sits at frame left).
Padmini's own horse is black with a white blaze on page 2 but brown with a blaze on page 1; her mount is not locked in the bible.
The thong-bound boots in this insert are a little taller, with the thongs in one band near the top, than the mid-calf spiral-bound pair in 2.4 and 12.1; same material and design family.
Nagoji's visible ear shows no gold stud at this small scale.

Varma's hair is loose and shoulder-length with no visible side knot above his left ear; the Nair chiefs wear their knots at the crown rather than front kudumi topknots; a small dark smudge on Ramayyan's bald crown; a stylus stands in a brass pot on the table (not in Ramayyan's hand). Beat delivered: Nagoji apart at the back, Varma on the low dais, Ramayyan cracking the seal on one ola.
Nagoji's ear ornament is a small bead at the very bottom of the lobe (about 4 px in a 2172 px frame); the distant soldiers at the fires are too small to tell their headwear.
The opened leaf Ramayyan lowers carries faint blurred horizontal strokes (no letterforms) and is a little broad for a palm leaf; Varma sits in a carved cushioned chair on the dais.
Varma holds a folded stack of leaves rather than the single strip of 6.3; faint scribble marks on the map sheet (not legible).
Nagoji's boots below the shrine steps read as modern lace-ups with eyelets and lug soles (fixed in chapter 9 to the sheet's thong-bound boots; not redrawn here).
On page 7 (7.1, 7.3, 7.5) the face zones of background guards, seated extras and figures seen from behind were dropped so the lettering could be placed; balloons may cover those background faces.

decided: 2026-10-02: Nagoji's ear ornament is the small flush gold stud (bible). From chapter 9 the prompts and selection enforce it; panels already picked in chapters 1 to 8 that show a small hanging drop are a known deviation, listed here for a later pass if wanted.

decided.decision: Chapter 9 page 4 split into two pages (4.1 to 4.3 stay; 4.4 and 4.5 become 5.1 and 5.2; pages 5 to 11 become 6 to 12). Later chapters' folios move by one.
Chapter 9: Nagoji rides Kayal, the bay. Padmini's sari stays cream per her sheet (bible base line aligned). Panel 12.3 mirrored so the brand is on his left forearm.
